newsitem.title: GERMANY: German finance ministry see 2.5 pct '97 GDP growth.
newsitem.headline: German finance ministry see 2.5 pct '97 GDP growth.

text.p: Germany's Finance Ministry still expects the economy to grow by 2.5 percent in 1997, and that unemployment will average 4.3 million this year, state secretary Hausgeorg Hauser said on Wednesday.

In the Bayernkurier newspaper, run by Finance Minister Theo Waigel's Christian Social Union (CSU), Hauser said the forecasts were based on continued implementation of structural reforms and budget consolidation.
"Current developments demand swift and decisive action," including vigorous efforts to privatise state enterprises, Hauser said.
That is why Waigel has proposed the sale of more Telekom shares this year, he said, adding that the interests of small shareholders would be protected.

Hauser also underscored Waigel's plan to revalue the Bundesbank's gold reserves closer to market levels, as part of an effort to meld European central banks. No gold will be sold, Hauser said, repeating comments made by Waigel last week.
